START / PATHWAY / STAGE HEADER
QUESTION to ask the patient
Patient’s answer → follow this arrow
HANDS-ON CHECK or TEST
EMERGENCY — act now or same day; no exercise
URGENT — doctor or specialist within days
SOON — check within about a week; gentle exercise can start
REFER — doctor or specialist within weeks; exercise alongside
SWITCH PATHWAY — the pain is coming from somewhere else
PASSED the safety screen
WORKING DIAGNOSIS + NEXT STEP
EXERCISE GROUP (square corners) — diagnoses that share a programme
CORE PROGRAMME — where every group ends up
MEASURE · DOSE · RE-TEST

KEY SOURCES (1 of 3) — low back: guidelines, red flags and diagnosis
KEY SOURCES (2 of 3) — neck and upper back
KEY SOURCES (3 of 3) — exercise, bone health, context
START
Q0 · Where is the main pain?
Low back, buttock or leg (below the lowest ribs)
Mid-back at the bottom of the ribs, or both regions, or not sure
Neck, head, top of the shoulder, between or over the shoulder blades, or down the arm
Use MOVEMENT to decide
LOW BACK PATHWAY
STAGE 1 — SAFETY SCREEN: Is this back pain safe to treat with exercise?
SAFETY MODIFIERS — not stops; they change who signs off and how hard you start
L1 · Cauda equina syndrome (pressure on the bundle of nerves at the bottom of the spine)
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
L2 · Spinal fracture after major injury
EMERGENCY
L3 · Spinal infection (bone or disc infection, epidural abscess)
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
L4 · Not from the spine — kidney, abdomen, pelvis or a swollen main artery (aortic aneurysm)
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
L5 · Severe or worsening nerve damage (progressive neurological deficit)
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
L6 · Fragility (osteoporotic) fracture of a spinal bone
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
L7 · Possible cancer in the spine
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
L8 · Spinal tuberculosis (Pott’s disease)
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
L9 · Child or teenager with back pain
SOON — WITHIN ABOUT A WEEK
L10 · Inflammatory back pain (axial spondyloarthritis)
REFER — WITHIN WEEKS
L11 · Pain coming from the hip (or from the hip AND the back)
SWITCH PATHWAY
L12 · Leg cramp when walking — poor artery circulation (vascular claudication)
REFER — ROUTINE
ALL 12 = NO → EXERCISE-RESPONSIVE (BY EXCLUSION)

HS3-1 · How irritable is the hip?
HIGH: night or rest pain; limping on most steps; flares with small movements; settles over hours or by the next day
MODERATE: pain with stairs, squatting or long walks; settles within an hour or two
LOW: pain only at high load or at the end of range; settles within minutes

STAGE 2 — WHICH HIP PROBLEM IS IT?
WHY THE LABEL MATTERS MORE AT THE HIP
HD1 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Hip osteoarthritis
Fits: weight-bearing pain, stiffness under 1 hour, limited or painful internal rotation
Rotation normal and the pain is on the side → side-of-hip check (HT3)
Younger than typical, with a risk factor (steroids, alcohol, sickle cell) → back to H5
HT1 · Hip osteoarthritis check (JOSPT hip osteoarthritis guideline, Cibulka 2017; revised 2025)
50 or older (from 45 if the pattern is typical)
HD2 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Hip-related pain — FAI syndrome, hip dysplasia or labral tear (Zurich consensus, Reiman 2020)
A) FADIR reproduces their groin pain
HD3 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Adductor-related groin pain
B) Squeeze or adductor tendon
HD4 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Iliopsoas-related groin pain
C) Resisted hip bending or stretch
HD5 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Inguinal-related groin pain
D) Sit-up, cough or inguinal canal — no lump
D) A lump that bulges on coughing → hernia, back to H9
HD6 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Pubic-related groin pain
E) Pubic bone tender
HT2 · Groin test set for active people (Doha agreement, Weir 2015)
16–49 and active (sport, heavy work)
Under 16 → back to H3 (child with a limp)
HQ2 · How old, and how active?
Groin or front of the hip (or the C-sign)
HD7 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Gluteal tendinopathy (side-of-hip pain; often called “trochanteric bursitis”)
Tender AND pain on single-leg stance (or another loading test)
Not tender on the bony point → check the hip joint (HT1) and the back (H10)
Burning or numbness rather than tenderness → HD8
HT3 · Side-of-hip check (gluteal tendinopathy — Grimaldi 2017, 65 patients compared with MRI)
Side of the hip, over the bony point
HD9 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Hamstring strain injury
Tender muscle + pain on resisted testing
Gap or big bruise at the sitting bone → back to H11
HT4 · Hamstring strain check (JOSPT hamstring guideline, Martin 2022)
Sudden pain at the back of the thigh while sprinting, kicking or over-stretching
HD10 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Proximal hamstring tendinopathy
Deep pain right at the sitting bone; worse on hard seats, uphill or bending forward
HX1 · SACROILIAC JOINT PAIN → LOW-BACK PATHWAY
3 or more of 6 positive
0–2 positive → deep gluteal (HD11)
HT5 · Sacroiliac joint check (the joint between the base of the spine and the pelvis) — Laslett cluster
Below the dimples of the low back; after pregnancy or a fall onto the buttock
HD11 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Deep gluteal syndrome (includes “piriformis syndrome”)
Deep buttock pain with sitting, sometimes sciatica-like, and everything else is negative
HQ3 · Buttock or back-of-thigh pain: how did it start, and where exactly?
Buttock, or the back of the upper thigh
HD8 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Meralgia paresthetica (squeezed skin nerve of the thigh)
Outer-front thigh: a burning, tingling or numb patch
HQ1 · Where does it hurt?
HIP PATHWAY
STAGE 1 — SAFETY SCREEN: Is this hip pain safe to treat with exercise?
H1 · Possible hip fracture
EMERGENCY
H2 · Hot, irritable hip — possible joint infection
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
H3 · Child or teenager with a limp
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
H4 · Stress fracture of the hip (femoral neck)
EMERGENCY — STOP IMPACT NOW
H5 · Possible avascular necrosis (bone death in the ball of the hip)
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
H6 · Possible tumour, or cancer spread to bone
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
H7 · Whole-body (inflammatory) or post-viral arthritis
REFER — WITHIN WEEKS
H8 · Possible tuberculosis (TB) of the hip
REFER
H9 · Not the hip: hernia, abdominal or pelvic organ
SWITCH PATHWAY
H10 · Pain coming from the lower back
SWITCH PATHWAY
H11 · Possible proximal hamstring avulsion (hamstring tendon torn off the sitting bone)
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
H12 · Buttock or thigh cramp when walking — poor artery circulation
REFER — ROUTINE
SAFETY MODIFIERS — not stops; they change who signs off and how hard you start
ALL 12 = NO → EXERCISE-RESPONSIVE (BY EXCLUSION)

HIGH: pain at rest or at night; flares with small movements; takes hours or until the next day to settle
MODERATE: pain with specific loads (stairs, squatting); settles within an hour or two
LOW: pain only at high load or at the end of activity; settles within minutes

START MODERATE

KS3-3 · ADD-ON MODULE — pick the one that matches the working diagnosis

KS3-4 · WEEK 1 — dose check
Yes — keep the same level (don’t level up yet)
No — hold or step down one level
KS3-5 · WEEK 4 — first re-test
Improving
Not improving
LEVEL UP
RE-CHECK BEFORE CONTINUING
KS3-6 · WEEK 12 — programme review
Yes — continue and move towards self-management

STAGE 2 — WHICH KNEE PROBLEM IS IT?
WHY THE LABEL MATTERS (OR DOESN’T)
KD1 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: ACL injury (torn anterior cruciate ligament)
Lachman OR lever sign positive
KN1 · Can’t clear the ACL yet
Too swollen or guarded to test properly
Both clearly negative in a relaxed knee → check the meniscus (KT2)
KT1 · Test the ACL (anterior cruciate ligament — the main ligament that stops the shin bone sliding forward)
Twisted or landed, felt or heard a POP, swelled within a few hours, couldn’t carry on
KD2 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Traumatic meniscus tear
3 or more of 5 positive
0–2 positive → check the side ligaments (KT3)
KT2 · Meniscus check — count how many of these 5 are positive (Lowery composite)
Twisted on a bent, loaded knee; swelling crept up over the next day; now it catches
KD3 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: MCL or LCL sprain (side-ligament sprain)
Painful or opens at 30° only
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
Opens even with the knee fully straight
KT3 · Side-ligament check — MCL (medial collateral ligament, inner side) and LCL (lateral collateral ligament, outer side)
Hit or pushed on the SIDE of the knee; pain on the inner or outer side
KD4 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: PCL injury (torn posterior cruciate ligament)
Sag or drawer positive
Negative → test the ACL and meniscus (KT1)
KT4 · Back-ligament check — PCL (posterior cruciate ligament — stops the shin sliding backward)
Fell onto a bent knee, or the shin hit a dashboard
KD5 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: First-time kneecap (patellar) dislocation
The kneecap slid out to the side (it may have popped back)
KQ2 · What happened at the moment of injury?
A specific injury — a fall, twist, blow or awkward landing
KD6 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Osgood-Schlatter (top of the shin) or Sinding-Larsen-Johansson (bottom tip of the kneecap)
A bony bump at the top of the shin just below the kneecap, or the bottom tip of the kneecap
Around or behind the kneecap → kneecap check (KT6)
KD7 · REFER FOR IMAGING: suspected osteochondritis dissecans
Vague pain with repeated swelling or catching, no clear injury
KQ4 · Child: where does it hurt?
Under 16 (still growing)
KD9 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Patellofemoral pain (pain from the joint behind the kneecap)
Squatting reproduces the pain
Squat is pain-free → recheck the spot (KT7)
KT6 · Kneecap-pain check (patellofemoral pain)
Around or behind the kneecap — hard to point to one spot
KD10 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Patellar tendinopathy (“jumper’s knee”)
Tender spot + load-related pain
Not tender, the pain is diffuse → kneecap check (KT6)
KT7 · Kneecap-tendon check (patellar tendinopathy)
One spot at the bottom edge of the kneecap
KD11 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Iliotibial band (ITB) syndrome
Tender above the joint line, distance-related pain
Joint-line tenderness and catching → meniscus check (KT2)
KT8 · Outer-knee check
Outer side of the knee
KD12 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Degenerative meniscus tear
Tender ON the joint line, middle-aged, catching
KD13 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Pes anserine pain
Tender BELOW the joint line on the inner shin
KT9 · Inner-side check
Inner side of the knee
KD14 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Prepatellar bursitis (“housemaid’s knee”)
Not hot, no fever
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
Hot, red, fever or a skin break
KT10 · Swelling on top of the kneecap — is it infected?
A soft swelling ON TOP of the kneecap (often from kneeling)
KD15 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Baker’s (popliteal) cyst
Back of the knee — fullness or tightness
KQ5 · Where does it hurt?
KD8 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Knee osteoarthritis (OA)
Fits: activity pain, stiffness 30 minutes or less
Stiffness over 30 minutes, warmth, or several swollen joints → back to K10
Doesn’t fit — the pain is in one specific spot → KQ5
KT5 · Osteoarthritis check (no X-ray needed)
45 or older
KQ3 · How old is the patient?
Gradually, with no clear injury
KD16 · WORKING DIAGNOSIS: Recurrent kneecap instability
Apprehension or J-sign positive
KT11 · Kneecap-instability check
The kneecap slips out sideways, or has dislocated before
Positive → same plan as KD1 (ACL injury)
KT12 · Old ACL tear check
The whole knee buckles when turning or pivoting, after an old injury
It gives way with pain or catching on the joint line → meniscus check (KT2)
KN2 · Giving way from weakness or pain
It gives way from weakness or pain; nothing slips (often older knees)
KQ6 · What gives way?
It keeps giving way, or the kneecap keeps slipping out
KQ1 · How did it start?
KNEE PATHWAY
STAGE 1 — SAFETY SCREEN: Is this knee pain safe to treat with exercise?
K1 · Possible broken bone (fracture)
EMERGENCY
K2 · Dislocated knee, or damage to the artery or nerve
EMERGENCY
K3 · Hot, red, swollen knee — possible joint infection (septic arthritis) or gout
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
K4 · Possible blood clot in the leg (deep vein thrombosis, DVT)
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
K5 · Can’t straighten the knee against gravity — torn quadriceps or kneecap tendon
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
K6 · Truly locked knee
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
K7 · Fast swelling after a twist, or the kneecap popped out
SOON — WITHIN ABOUT A WEEK
K8 · Child or teen: a HIP problem showing up as knee pain
EMERGENCY — SAME DAY
K9 · Possible tumour or serious bone disease
URGENT — WITHIN DAYS
K10 · Whole-body (inflammatory) or post-viral arthritis
REFER — WITHIN WEEKS
K11 · Possible tuberculosis (TB) of the knee
REFER
K12 · Pain coming from the back or the hip (referred pain)
SWITCH PATHWAY
K13 · Calf or thigh cramp when walking — poor artery circulation
REFER — ROUTINE
SAFETY MODIFIERS — not stops; they change who signs off and how hard you start
ALL 13 = NO → EXERCISE-RESPONSIVE (BY EXCLUSION)
